transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-30 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Head of MLOps, Bluewater), Rosa Chen (CTO, Bluewater), Samir Patel (Infra Lead, Bluewater)

AutoSummary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Discussed renewal + expansion: moving from hosted to Dedicated reserved pools, adding APAC region, potential 24-month contract extension. Action items include pricing, SOC2/VPC docs, APAC benchmark.

00:00 Ben Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 40 minutes, quick agenda — renewals, capacity, and APAC region.
00:12 Liam O'Connor: Thanks Ben, appreciate it. We wanted to lock down numbers so finance can start the extension review.
00:20 Maya Singh: Hi all, I'll be covering the technical bits, sizing, and what dedicated looks like operationally — sorry if my audio is a little off, new headset.
00:34 Rosa Chen: No worries. Quick context: we've been on hosted for 11 months, steady growth, but Q3 forecast pushes token usage up 3-4x and we need predictable latency in APAC.
00:48 Ben Carter: Right — congrats on the growth. Today we'll go through a recommended Dedicated configuration, burst options, and how adding an APAC region affects costs and latency. Also discuss term options, e.g., 12 vs 24 month.
01:05 Samir Patel: On the infra side we care about VPC peering, audit logs to our SIEM, and KMS integration. We had a security review last quarter and want those items nailed down before commit.
01:18 Maya Singh: Yep, Bluewater — we can do a Private VPC or dedicated within our hosted offering, depends on compliance. VPC/private control plane supports customer-managed KMS, and audit logs are available for 90/365 retention per plan.
01:35 Liam O'Connor: Quick question: if we go Dedicated, do we still get automatic fallback to hosted instances if Dedicated is at capacity?
01:44 Maya Singh: Good q — yes, we support policy-based routing: you can set strict dedicated-only or allow fallback to compatible hosted variants. If strict, requests will queue or error when capacity is exhausted; with fallback we route to a lower-tier model. There is a small cost delta and variance in latency.
01:58 Ben Carter: To frame options: baseline Dedicated (4xA100 equiv) covers your current peaks, burst to 6x for seasonal spikes, and APAC region adds an additional pool; pricing shows ~25% uplift for region + burst.
02:15 Rosa Chen: The 25% uplift — is that for reserved capacity or on-demand?
02:21 Ben Carter: That's committed reserved pricing. On-demand in APAC would be higher. We can model blended rates if you want tiered usage.
02:30 Liam O'Connor: For latency, our 95th pct target in APAC is under 180ms end-to-end. Can Redwood meet that from Singapore region?
02:42 Maya Singh: In our internal benchmarks, Singapore region with a local Dedicated pool gets ~120-160ms for 2k token responses; but real numbers depend on request size and KV cache hit rates. We should run a short APAC benchmark with your request distribution.
02:58 Samir Patel: That would be ideal. Also we need SOC2 docs — last time we saw a partial report. Can you share the full attestation plus network diagrams?
03:10 Ben Carter: Absolutely — I'll share SOC 2 Type II and the VPC architecture whitepaper after the call. Maya will include KMS integration notes.
03:20 Rosa Chen: Great. On contract term — finance prefers 24 months if we can get a better blended rate and a cap on yearly price increases. Is that possible?
03:31 Ben Carter: Yes, for 24-month we can offer a ~10% discount on committed capacity and a price cap clause for compute costs (excludes pass-through cloud egress). We can draft two quote options.
03:45 Liam O'Connor: One of the blockers from procurement is audit logging retention beyond 90 days. We may need 12 months. Is that an add-on?
03:55 Maya Singh: Longer retention is available as an add-on to the observability tier; we'll include pricing in the quote. There may be some uplift for storage and retention pipeline.
04:10 Ben Carter: Okay, quick tech deep-dive — Samir, can you share current p95 numbers from your hosted usage?
04:18 Samir Patel: Right now our p95 in US is ~95ms for short prompts, long prompts spike to ~450ms occasionally during peak. We use caching at the app layer but want tighter tail latencies.
04:31 Maya Singh: Those long tail spikes sound like cache misses + batching. We can tune batching and prefix KV cache; Dedicated gives more predictable tail since you control pool size and there are kernel optimizations we enable on that runtime.
04:47 Liam O'Connor: How disruptive is migrating a route from hosted to dedicated? We have multiregion traffic split.
04:55 Maya Singh: Minimal — routes are config-driven. We do canary rollouts and traffic shaping. For multiregion you can pin model versions and use smart routing to keep latency targets. We'll propose a migration plan: small % canary, step to 50%, then full cutoff.
05:18 Ben Carter: For the APAC benchmark, we'll need a representative prompt set and your token size distro. Liam, can you share a 24-48 hour sample traffic dump?
05:27 Liam O'Connor: Yes, we'll scrub PII and share next week.
05:33 Rosa Chen: Anything else on compliance? SAML/SSO and RBAC are must-haves.
05:40 Maya Singh: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC at route and model level. We'll include screenshots and the admin guide.
05:55 Ben Carter: Let's talk numbers — Maya, can you remind us the capacity tiers and estimated cost delta moving to Dedicated + APAC?
06:03 Maya Singh: Sure — baseline reserved Dedicated for your usage (4xA100 equiv) is $X/month (placeholder on call), burst to 6x adds ~40% to capacity priced at a lower incremental rate. APAC region pool is approx 25% uplift on top because of region egress and on-demand buffer. Full quote will itemize compute, storage, observability retention, and premium SLAs.
06:28 Rosa Chen: We'll need the quote broken out: compute, observability, audit retention, and professional services for migration.
06:35 Ben Carter: Noted. We'll send two quotes: 12-month and 24-month, with add-ons broken out.
06:42 Samir Patel: One last technical: do you provide customer-controlled KMS keys in Dedicated?
06:48 Maya Singh: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (bring your own KMS) and HSM via partner integrations for on-prem/private deployments.
06:55 Liam O'Connor: Great — timeline wise, if we sign by mid-April, when could APAC Dedicated be live?
07:02 Maya Singh: Typically provisioning + validation is 3-4 weeks for a new region Dedicated pool, assuming the benchmark and test pass. So mid-May is feasible if we start mid-April.
07:12 Ben Carter: Okay to recap next steps?
07:15 Rosa Chen: Yes please.
07:18 Ben Carter: Action items: Ben will send revised quote with 12/24 month options and breakout, Maya will share SOC2, VPC/KMS docs and APAC benchmark plan, Bluewater to share traffic sample and confirm SLA targets. We'll tentatively schedule benchmark week of 2026-04-06.
07:35 Liam O'Connor: That looks good. Thanks everyone.
07:38 Ben Carter: Thanks, we'll follow up over email with the docs and next meeting invite.

(Transcript ends — automated timestamps approximate. Some words may be mis-transcribed, e.g., product names or acronyms.)
